ops.old:
The best luxury cruise in Halong Bay is the one that fits your trip: the right bay, enough nights, a route that reaches quieter corners, a cabin you will actually use and terms you can live with. These 12 questions help you compare any two boats on facts rather than adjectives.

[IMAGE: An overnight cruise ship at anchor among limestone karsts on Ha Long Bay in soft morning light | alt: Overnight cruise ship anchored among limestone islands on Ha Long Bay]

A note before you read: We operate Green Ruby Cruises, so we use our own ships as examples where they illustrate a point, and we say so when we do. Green Ruby is not sailing yet. Both ships are expected to enter service in February 2027, a provisional date, and there are no prices or guest reviews to quote. If you are planning a Halong Bay luxury cruise in 2026, the questions below apply to any boat, but Green Ruby will not be one of your options. The Green Ruby brand facts page sets out the company details and current status.

What makes the best luxury cruise in Halong Bay?

If you search for the best 5-star cruise in Halong Bay, you will find the label on a lot of boats. On its own it tells you little. Ask who awarded the rating and what it covers, then test the boat against the questions below. If a boat is sold as 6-star, treat that as marketing: Vietnam has no official 6-star rating.

What separates a good luxury cruise from an expensive one is usually practical. Time on the water rather than in a minibus. Stops at hours when fewer day boats are around. A cabin with room to sit, and clear terms when the weather turns. The twelve questions follow the order in which most people make the decision.

1. Ha Long Bay or Lan Ha Bay: which water suits you?

Ha Long Bay is the classic choice. It has the views that appear in most photos of the area, large caves such as Sung Sot, and the busiest water. Lan Ha Bay lies to the south, near Cat Ba Island. The limestone scenery is similar, with fewer boats, quieter anchorages and more beaches and lagoons for swimming and kayaking.

Our advice is simple. If this is your one visit and you want the well-known Ha Long views, choose Ha Long. If you dislike crowds, or you care more about time in a kayak than about famous caves, choose Lan Ha.

With Green Ruby, choosing the bay means choosing the ship. Green Ruby 1 sails Ha Long Bay. Its sister ship, Green Ruby 2, is built to the same design and sails Lan Ha Bay.

2. Two days and one night, or three days and two nights?

A 2-day, 1-night cruise gives you one afternoon and one morning on the bay. You board around midday, have a cave or kayak stop and a sunset, sleep at anchor, then fit one activity in before brunch and the return to port. It works when your schedule is tight. Remember that the drive back to Hanoi is as long as the drive out, so one night means a lot of road for a short stay.

The second night changes the trip more than the extra hours suggest. On a typical three-day programme, the ship stays at anchor while a smaller day boat takes you further out, to quieter corners the two-day route does not reach. You also get a full day without packing, checking in or checking out.

On Green Ruby, the Halong Immersion, 3 days 2 nights uses its day boat for Cua Van floating village, Tien Ong Cave and a pearl farm. On Lan Ha Bay, the Lan Ha Immersion, 3 days 2 nights spends day two at Viet Hai village, reached on foot, by bike or by buggy, with lunch in the village and a swim at a white-sand beach.

Green Ruby itineraryShip and bayLengthMain stops
The Halong EscapeGreen Ruby 1, Ha Long Bay2 days 1 nightLuon Cave by kayak or bamboo boat, Ti Top Island, Sung Sot Cave
The Halong ImmersionGreen Ruby 1, Ha Long Bay3 days 2 nightsLuon Cave, Ti Top Island, Cua Van Fishing Village, Tien Ong Cave, pearl farm, Sung Sot Cave
The Lan Ha EscapeGreen Ruby 2, Lan Ha Bay2 days 1 nightDark & Bright Cave area by kayak or bamboo boat, Ao Ech Lagoon
The Lan Ha ImmersionGreen Ruby 2, Lan Ha Bay3 days 2 nightsDark & Bright Cave, Viet Hai village, white-sand beach, a cave visit on day three

If your dates allow it, take two nights. The transfer is the same length either way, and the second night is when the quieter parts of the bay come into the trip.

3. Which official route will the boat follow?

Boats on Ha Long Bay do not choose their own course. They sail numbered sightseeing routes set by the authorities, and the route decides which caves, islands and villages you can visit. Two boats both selling "Ha Long Bay" can show you quite different parts of it. Lan Ha Bay belongs to Hai Phong and has its own arrangements, so ask about it separately.

A sightseeing fee is set for each route, so it does not depend on which boat you choose. Rates change by official decision, and the Ha Long Bay Management Board publishes notices such as the one on fees for three sightseeing routes on Ha Long Bay. Check the current figure before you travel rather than trusting an old blog post. Then ask any operator two things: which route the boat uses, and whether the fee is in the fare.

Green Ruby includes all sightseeing entrance fees in the fare. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: tuyến tham quan mà Green Ruby 1 và Green Ruby 2 sử dụng, và xác nhận phí tham quan của các tuyến này đã bao gồm trong giá]

4. Where do you board, and how long is the transfer from Hanoi?

Many overnight cruises check in at Tuan Chau in Ha Long. Ask whether the boat uses a public terminal or its own lounge, what time check-in opens, how you reach the ship, and where the cruise ends. The last point matters on Lan Ha Bay, where boarding and return points can differ.

For Green Ruby, check-in is at the Green Ruby lounge at Tuan Chau around 10:45, with embarkation at 11:45. Green Ruby 1 guests take a tender to the ship on Ha Long Bay. Green Ruby 2 guests take a tender to Gia Luan Pier in Hai Phong and board on Lan Ha Bay. On the Lan Ha Escape, 2 days 1 night, the programme ends with a transfer back to Tuan Chau and disembarkation around 11:00. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: cách khách Green Ruby 2 quay về Tuần Châu khi kết thúc (tàu, tender hay xe qua Gia Luận)]

The published Green Ruby itineraries plan an 08:00 departure from Hanoi, and the drive takes about 2.5 hours. Transfers are not part of the cruise fare: a shared limousine shuttle or a private car can be arranged at extra cost. If you land on an early or late flight, share the details so the transfer can be timed around it.

5. What is the cabin actually like?

Ask for numbers, not mood photos. Floor area in square metres is the most honest figure. Then ask whether the sea view comes through a window or from a private balcony, how the beds are set up, whether there is a bathtub, and whether a third person can sleep in the cabin.

Green Ruby has the same four categories on both ships. Serenity Deluxe and Ocean Breeze Premium are 38 m² for up to two guests, each with a bathtub and separate shower. The Royal Romance Suite is 80 m² for two, with a Jacuzzi bathtub and a private terrace. The Imperial Suite on Green Ruby 1 is 120 m² for up to three guests, with a balcony Jacuzzi and a terrace. The number of cabins in each category is not published. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: tất cả các hạng cabin đều có ban công riêng hay không]

For a couple on a one-night cruise, 38 m² with a bathtub is plenty. A suite makes more sense on a three-day cruise, when you have afternoons on board to use the terrace. Families should ask about extra beds early: they can be added to selected cabins, with a surcharge.

[IMAGE: Interior of a 38 m² cabin with bed facing the window, bathtub visible, bay view outside | alt: Cruise cabin with bathtub and view of limestone islands]

6. How many guests share the ship and the activities?

Guest numbers shape the trip more than décor does. On board, the ratio of guests to deck space decides whether you find a quiet seat at sunset. On excursions, what counts is how many people share each tender, kayak launch and cave visit. Ask for the maximum number of guests, how the group is split for excursions, and whether there are enough kayaks for everyone at once.

Each Green Ruby ship is 121 m long, with four decks, 46 cabins and room for up to 136 guests. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: số khách tối đa mỗi nhóm kayak, tender và day boat]

7. What is included, and what will you pay for on board?

"All inclusive" means different things on different boats. Get a written list that answers each of these:

  • Meals: how many, and whether the last-day brunch is counted.
  • Guide: included or not, and in which language.
  • Kayaks and bamboo boats: included or charged per use.
  • Sightseeing fees: in the fare or paid on the day.
  • Drinks: what is free and what comes from the bar menu.
  • Transfers from Hanoi, spa treatments and tipping.

For Green Ruby, the fare covers all meals in the itinerary, a private air-conditioned cabin, sightseeing entrance fees, kayaking and bamboo boat activities, the cooking class and morning Tai Chi, an English or Vietnamese-speaking guide, and the day boat excursion on day two of the three-day itineraries. Not included: beverages other than drinking water, spa treatments, Hanoi transfers and personal expenses. Tipping is at your discretion. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: hành trình Lan Ha Escape có bao gồm hướng dẫn viên tiếng Anh không]

8. How much time goes on activities, and at what time of day?

Read the timetable, not the highlights list. Count the activity stops, note when each one happens and ask how long it lasts. Large caves draw day boats as well as overnight cruises, so the hour of your visit affects how crowded it feels. Also ask whether kayaking is guided or free paddling.

As an example, the Halong Escape, 2 days 1 night reaches Luon Cave at 15:30 and Ti Top Island at 16:30, where you can swim or climb to the viewpoint. Sunset follows at 17:30, the evening includes a cooking class and squid fishing, and Sung Sot Cave comes at 08:00 the next morning, before brunch. On the Lan Ha Escape, the Dark & Bright Cave area comes at 15:30 by kayak or bamboo boat, and Ao Ech Lagoon at 07:45 on day two.

Sung Sot is large and popular, so it is worth asking what time your boat goes in. The same applies to any cave on your list.

[IMAGE: Guests in kayaks paddling through a low limestone arch into a calm lagoon on Lan Ha Bay | alt: Kayaks entering a lagoon through a limestone arch on Lan Ha Bay]

9. How does the boat handle safety and bad weather?

The bay has two broad seasons. October to April is cooler and drier and is the most popular period; October, November, March and April are usually the most comfortable. Winter evenings on deck are cool, so pack a warm layer. May to September is warm and good for swimming, but it is also storm season, and the authorities can restrict sailing at short notice.

Before you book, ask what happens if the authorities close the bay on your date: refund, new date or a replacement service. Ask whether there is a safety briefing on boarding, whether life jackets are provided for every water activity, and what medical help is on board.

Green Ruby's policy: if local authorities restrict sailing because of weather or other force majeure, guests may receive a full refund, an alternative departure date or a suitable replacement service, depending on the circumstances. The safety briefing is at 12:30 on boarding day, life jackets are provided for kayaking and swimming, and trained crew with first aid equipment handle minor issues, with transfer to shore for anything serious. Any onboard cover is not personal travel insurance, so arrange your own for the whole trip.

10. How green is the ship, really?

If you are asking what is the best sustainable luxury cruise in Halong Bay, a brochure alone cannot answer it. Three checks separate real claims from slogans. Is the figure measured or a design estimate? Is the certification in progress or awarded, and by which standard? Is wastewater treated before discharge, or not discharged at all? The same goes for plastics: "being removed" and "plastic-free" are not the same claim.

Here is how Green Ruby answers those checks:

  • A rooftop solar array of about 70 kW on each ship (design specification), estimated to avoid about 60 tonnes of CO₂ a year (design estimate).
  • Air conditioning cooled with seawater. Solar and seawater cooling together are designed to cut onboard energy use by around 40% (design estimate for both combined).
  • A heat recovery system that reuses waste heat from the engines and generators for hot water and climate control.
  • 100% of wastewater biologically treated on board before discharge. That is treatment, not zero discharge.
  • No hybrid propulsion.
  • Single-use plastics are being removed from guest service. This is work in progress.
  • Green Globe certification, a GSTC-accredited standard, is in progress. Green Ruby is not certified.

Measured emissions data does not exist yet, because the ships are not in service. The Green Ruby eco dashboard explains the methods and current status. For the wider picture, including what to ask any operator, see our complete guide to eco-friendly luxury cruises in Ha Long Bay.

[IMAGE: Rooftop solar panels on the upper deck of a cruise ship with limestone islands behind | alt: Solar panels on the roof deck of a cruise ship on Ha Long Bay]

11. Can the crew handle dietary needs, children and limited mobility?

Raise special requests at booking, not at check-in, because the kitchen stocks before the ship leaves. Ask specific questions. For halal food, ask whether the kitchen is certified or whether dishes are prepared on request. For children, ask about age bands for pricing and whether they can join kayaking. For limited mobility, ask about lifts, tender transfers and steps on excursions.

On Green Ruby, vegetarian, vegan and allergy-conscious menus can be prepared with advance notice, as can Korean and Japanese dishes. Green Ruby is applying for Halal certification: Halal certification in progress, not yet awarded. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: tổ chức chứng nhận Halal, phạm vi (bếp hay toàn tàu), thời gian dự kiến, phòng cầu nguyện, chính sách đồ uống có cồn, phục vụ iftar/suhoor, đào tạo nhân viên]

Families are welcome. Kayaking and swimming use calm, sheltered water, life jackets are provided, crew guide beginners, and children must be with an adult. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: chính sách giá trẻ em (lịch trình ghi dưới 2 tuổi miễn phí, 5 đến 11 tuổi 75%; FAQ ghi 0 đến 4 tuổi miễn phí, giá riêng cho 5 đến 10 tuổi)] There is lift access between guest decks, but some excursions involve steps, tender transfers or uneven ground, such as the climb at Ti Top Island.

12. What are the booking terms?

Read the deposit, the balance date, the cancellation scale and the rules for changes before you pay anything. Keep weather-related changes separate in your mind from your own cancellations: they are usually handled under different rules.

Green Ruby's cancellation scale:

When you cancelCharge
30 days or more before departureFull refund
15 to 29 days before50% charge
7 to 14 days before75% charge
Under 7 days, or no-showNo refund

A 30% deposit confirms the booking, with the balance due 30 days before departure. Bookings made within 30 days of departure are paid in full. A date change counts as a cancellation and a new booking, and each booking can be amended twice at most. For peak periods (October to April, holidays and weekends), our reservations team suggests booking 2 to 3 months ahead. There are no published prices yet; quotes come from the reservations team. The details are collected in the bookings and payments FAQ.

A printable version of this checklist is available to download. [CẦN XÁC NHẬN: link tải checklist]

Frequently asked questions

Is Lan Ha Bay part of the UNESCO World Heritage site?

Yes. In September 2023 UNESCO extended the Ha Long Bay site to include the Cat Ba Archipelago, where Lan Ha Bay lies. The site, now listed as Ha Long Bay-Cat Ba Archipelago, covers 65,650 ha and 1,133 islands and islets across Quang Ninh Province and Hai Phong City.

Will I get seasick?

Most people do not. The water is sheltered by thousands of limestone islands and is usually calm. If you are sensitive to motion, bring a remedy as a precaution.

What should I pack?

Light clothing, swimwear, sunglasses, sun protection, a hat, comfortable shoes for cave paths and island climbs, any personal medication and your passport, which Green Ruby's itineraries ask guests to bring. In winter, add a warm layer for evenings on deck.

Can I charter a whole ship?

On Green Ruby, yes. A full ship can be reserved for families, celebrations or corporate groups, and the route can be adjusted within the bay's navigation rules and the weather.

Once you have the answers in hand, the best luxury cruise in Halong Bay is the one whose details you can check in writing before you pay. If Green Ruby suits your dates, you can compare all itineraries side by side. When you are ready, talk to our reservations team about the bay and cabin you have in mind.

Here is how Green Ruby answers those checks:

  • Design specification: a rooftop solar array of about 70 kW on each ship.
  • Design specification: air conditioning cooled with seawater, and a heat recovery system that reuses waste heat from the engines and generators for hot water and climate control.
  • Engineering estimate: solar power and seawater cooling together are designed to reduce onboard energy use by around 40% compared with a conventional reference. The calculation behind this figure has not been published, and it is not a measured result.
  • Design specification: 100% of wastewater biologically treated on board before discharge. That is treatment, not zero discharge.
  • Work in progress: single-use plastics are being removed from guest service.
  • Certification: Green Ruby has begun the Green Globe certification process. It is not certified; the on-site audit can only take place once a ship is operating.
  • No hybrid propulsion.

There are no operational measurements yet, because the ships are not in service. The Green Ruby eco dashboard explains what will be reported and how. For the wider picture, including what to ask any operator, see our guide to eco-friendly luxury cruises in Ha Long Bay.

11. Can the crew handle dietary needs, children and limited mobility?

Raise special requests at booking, not at check-in, because the kitchen stocks before the ship leaves. Ask specific questions. For Halal food, ask how it is prepared and whether any certification has actually been issued. For children, ask about age bands for pricing and which activities they can join. For limited mobility, ask about lifts, tender transfers and steps on excursions.

On Green Ruby, vegetarian and vegan menus, and menus for food allergies, are prepared with advance notice, as are Korean and Japanese dishes. Send allergy details before you board. Green Ruby plans to offer Halal dining prepared in dedicated Halal kitchen facilities, together with a prayer room for Muslim guests. The company is working with HALCERT on Halal certification, which has not yet been awarded. Tell the reservations team about any dietary or religious requirements when you book.

Families are welcome. Children must be accompanied by an adult, life jackets will be provided for water activities, and swimming takes place only when conditions allow. Child rates are confirmed by the reservations team when you book, so ask for them in writing. The ships are designed with lift access between guest decks, but several excursions involve stairs, tender boarding or uneven ground, such as the climb at Ti Top Island and the paths inside large caves.

12. What are the booking terms?

Read the deposit, the balance date, the cancellation scale and the rules for changes before you pay anything. Keep weather-related changes separate in your mind from your own cancellations: they are usually handled under different rules.

Green Ruby's cancellation scale:

A change of date counts as a cancellation and a new booking, and a standard booking can be amended up to two times. Deposit and balance rules depend on how far ahead you book, so check the current Booking Terms and Conditions and the amount shown when you pay, rather than relying on a summary. For peak periods (October to April, holidays and weekends), the reservations team suggests booking two to three months ahead. There are no published prices yet; quotes come from the reservations team. Common questions are answered in the bookings and payments FAQ.

Frequently asked questions

Is Lan Ha Bay part of the UNESCO World Heritage site?

Yes. In September 2023 UNESCO extended the Ha Long Bay site to include the Cat Ba Archipelago, where Lan Ha Bay lies. The site, now listed as Ha Long Bay-Cat Ba Archipelago, covers 65,650 ha and 1,133 islands and islets across Quang Ninh Province and Hai Phong City.

Will I get seasick?

It depends on the weather and on you. The bays are sheltered by limestone islands and are usually calmer than the open sea, but wind and season change conditions, and some people feel motion even on calm water. If you are sensitive to motion, bring a remedy as a precaution.

Can I go kayaking?

On Ha Long Bay, Green Ruby's itineraries plan Luon Cave by kayak or bamboo boat, subject to the rules in force and the weather on the day. On Lan Ha Bay, kayak services have been suspended since 15 November 2024, and we know of no official notice lifting the suspension as of October 2026. Bamboo boat visits are planned instead on Green Ruby 2.

What should I pack?

Light clothing, swimwear, sunglasses, sun protection, a hat, comfortable shoes for cave paths and island climbs, any personal medication and your passport, which Green Ruby's itineraries ask guests to bring. In winter, add a warm layer for evenings on deck.

Can I charter a whole ship?

Green Ruby plans to offer full-ship charters for families, celebrations and corporate groups, quoted individually. The route can be adjusted within the bay's navigation rules and the weather.

If Green Ruby suits your dates, you can compare all itineraries side by side. When you are ready, talk to our reservations team about the bay and cabin you have in mind.
